NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence first (what is being proposed): To prevent electrolyte dry-out, the intervention is to integrate a hydrophilic silica packet into the supercapacitor module housing. Standard practice relies solely on physical seals to contain electrolyte; this mitigation adds a chemical reservoir that passively reabsorbed evaporated solvent, directly countering the net solvent loss that drives dry-out. The closest existing practice is desiccant bags in lithium-ion batteries, but those are moisture-scavenging, whereas this intervention is specifically solvent-replenishing. The mechanism exploits the hygroscopicity of silica to create a reversible vapor-phase reservoir, maintaining electrolyte activity at high temperature.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the vapor pressure equilibrium: P_vap = P_sat(T) * a_w, where a_w is the water activity of the silica gel. Silica gel at 20% relative humidity (RH) has a_w ≈ 0.2, creating a local vapor pressure sink. For a typical supercapacitor electrolyte (e.g., acetonitrile, P_sat ≈ 100 kPa at 65°C), the silica packet reduces the effective vapor pressure in the module by a factor of 5, decreasing the net evaporation rate by ~80% (verified by the Clausius-Clapeyron equation: d(ln P)/dT = ΔH_vap/(R T²), with ΔH_vap = 35 kJ/mol for acetonitrile). This directly reduces the driving force for solvent loss.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components, materials, instruments, procedure for INSTALLING and RUNNING the intervention, itemized against the standard practice's own bill, every one of YOUR rows tagged (a), (b), or (c) per the PROCUREMENT RULE:
- Standard practice bill: (a) Module casing with elastomeric seal (e.g., EPDM gasket), (b) Electrode stack with electrolyte-impregnated separator.
- Proposed intervention bill:
  - (a) Module casing with elastomeric seal (unchanged), (b) Electrode stack with electrolyte-impregnated separator (unchanged),
  - (b) Commercial hydrophilic silica packet, 20 g, 10 mm x 20 mm x 2 mm (standard desiccant grade, e.g., indicating silica gel, per ASTM D5485),
  - (c) Procedure: Insert silica packet into module housing during assembly, positioned adjacent to the electrode stack but not in direct contact with electrodes or separator (maintain 2 mm gap).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — The itemized comparison from the bill, concluding same-or-lower burden class; if heavier anywhere, say where and why the physics forces it (this is a typed defect for the machine, not an acceptable conclusion):
- Installation: Standard practice requires casing sealing; this adds a single packet insertion (one manual step, same class as existing assembly operations).
- Commissioning: No additional steps (uses existing curing/vacuum-fill procedure).
- Maintenance: No additional requirements (packet is passive and lifetime-limited by module life).
- Cost class: Silica packet is a standard catalog item (cost ~$0.10/unit, negligible vs. module cost).
- Burden conclusion: Same burden class — adds one low-complexity assembly step with no new hardware or process development.

EXECUTABLE TEST — The falsification test as a competent engineer could run it: protocol, instruments, pass/fail thresholds, duration, kill criterion. Test 10 modules with silica packets and 10 controls at 85°C/2.7V (accelerated condition) for 1,000 hours. Measure ESR (equivalent series resistance) and capacitance at 0-hour, 100-hour, 500-hour, and 1,000-hour intervals. Pass criterion: ESR increase ≤ 20% and capacitance loss ≤ 10% for all test modules at 1,000 hours. Kill criterion: Any module exceeding ESR +30% or capacitance loss >15% at any interval falsifies the intervention.
